title: Knowledge check: Understanding Vue Directives

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Understanding Vue Directives”?
options: Manually rewrite the DOM for every state change.
Put multi-step business logic directly in template expressions.
Use raw HTML rendering for every value.
Use declarative template bindings and keep expressions small; choose directives according to the intended DOM behavior.
questions.answer_key: Use declarative template bindings and keep expressions small; choose directives according to the intended DOM behavior.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Understanding Vue Directives directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “How directives work”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Put multi-step business logic directly in template expressions.
Use raw HTML rendering for every value.
Use declarative template bindings and keep expressions small; choose directives according to the intended DOM behavior.
Manually rewrite the DOM for every state change.
questions.answer_key: Use declarative template bindings and keep expressions small; choose directives according to the intended DOM behavior.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “How directives work”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Understanding Vue Directives” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
